title: perf-bench-scratch-maya-lopez-2026-03-25
content:
Quick scratchpad for latency/throughput runs on l2-13b (q4) — notes to self.

Test environment:
- Date: 2026-03-25 (runs repeated 2026-03-26)
- Machine: Dedicated test rig (NVIDIA A100 80GB, 8 vCPU host), Ubuntu 22.04
- Runtime: serving-runtime @ main (PR 1234 local build)
- Model: redwood/l2-13b-8k-q4 (quantized FP16->q4 run)
- Sequence lengths: prompt 32 tokens, generate 256 tokens (total 288)
- Request patterns: single-request latency and sustained throughput (50 concurrent clients with ramp)
- Warmup: 50 warmup requests (to populate KV cache) before measurement

Commands used (local perf harness):
- ./perf_client --model l2-13b-q4 --prompt-file prompts.txt --max-tokens 256 --batch-size B --concurrency C --duration 120s
- curl to hosted-like endpoint for single-shot checks: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"model":"l2-13b-q4","prompt":"<short>","max_tokens":256}'

Runs summary (cold vs warm cache, batch sizes):
- Cold KV cache (first inference after model load):
  batch=1, concurrency=1 -> p50 420ms, p90 1.4s, p99 2.8s, tokens/s ~40
- Warm KV cache after warmup:
  batch=1, concurrency=1 -> p50 95ms, p90 130ms, p99 220ms, tokens/s ~220
  batch=4, concurrency=4 -> p50 120ms (per request), aggregate tokens/s ~820
  batch=8, concurrency=8 -> p50 200ms (per request), aggregate tokens/s ~1500 (good util but higher tail)

Observed patterns:
- KV cache warmup is huge: cold first-token latency dominated by model load + kernel init (~350-400ms). After warm, p50 drops ~4x.
- Small batches (1/4) give best p50 for interactive workloads; larger batches increase aggregate throughput but increase p99 tail.
- Concurrency scaling: up to concurrency 8 we see near-linear throughput gains for batch sizes >=4; above 16 concurrency we see scheduler queueing and p99 spikes.

Representative run (warm cache, batch=4, conc=4, 120s):
- avg latency (request->first-token): 125ms
- p50: 120ms, p90: 200ms, p99: 420ms
- throughput: 820 tokens/s (measured at runtime, accounting for prompt+gen)
- GPU util: 68-78% during steady-state

Micro notes / hypotheses:
- Kernel selection overhead seems amortized after first few steps but still shows small spikes when sequence length changes.
- GC / allocator pressure: noticed occasional 2-3x latency spikes aligned with host memory reclaim on the node; need to check oom_killer/syslogs.
- Batching/coscheduling: serving-runtime scheduler currently groups by arrival window; try moving to shape-aware batching to reduce p99 for mixed-length workloads.

Quick conclusions / guidance:
- For low-latency interactive: prefer batch=1 or 4, concurrency <=8. KV cache warmup must be accounted for on cold start (use pre-warm for critical endpoints).
- For throughput-first (background generation): batch=8+ with concurrency tuned to GPU memory bandwidth gives best tokens/s.
- Put model hot paths behind a warm pool (keep models loaded in dedicated pool) to avoid cold-load latencies for first requests.

TODOs / next steps:
- Run controlled experiment varying sequence length (128/256/512) to map latency vs seq length more precisely.
- Add perf traces (async stack traces) to capture allocator pauses and kernel selection timing.
- Re-run after PR 1234 kernel caching patch lands (expect ~10-15% tail reduction).
- Create a small dashboard widget in Console showing cold-start vs warm-start latency percentiles per model.

Notes to self (messy):
- Compare with rina's numbers from 2026-03-18 (she saw p99 ~380ms for batch=4, may be setup diff) 
- Slack convo: #eng-serving-runtime thread "kv-cache-warmups" — check pinned messages for warm-up script

Raw logs snippets (truncated):
- [2026-03-25T15:03:12Z] PERF INFO: req=1294 batch=4 conc=4 first_token_ms=118 total_tokens=256
- [2026-03-25T15:03:13Z] PERF INFO: req=1295 batch=4 conc=4 first_token_ms=122 total_tokens=256

If anyone picks this up: check JIRA-MLINF-342 for context and PR 1234 for recent runtime changes. Ping Ethan or Sam for help reproducing on dedicated QA cluster.

End of scratchpad.
